schema.description: Optional provenance for your integration. Lets you correlate this API call with records and logs in your own systems.

source.description: Human- or machine-readable name of the calling product or channel (for example your app name or partner integration ID).

sourceRequestId.description: Identifier of the originating object or request in your system (for example a CRM opportunity ID or ticket number). Useful when debugging or aligning with Vendr support.

sourceRequestUrl.description: URL of the originating request in your system (for example a CRM opportunity URL or ticket URL).

parameters.description: Additional structured supplier. Use the documented fields.
parameters.name: supplier

schema.description: The software vendor this negotiation is about. Must match Vendr’s catalog: send a catalog `id` when you have it, or a `name` when you want the service to resolve the supplier from text. At least one of `id` or `name` is required.

id.description: Catalog supplier UUID from Vendr catalog APIs (for example from company or product responses). Prefer this when you already store the canonical supplier id.

name.description: Supplier name as known to the buyer (for example company or product brand). Used for catalog lookup when `id` is not supplied; resolution works best when the name clearly matches a single catalog entry.

parameters.description: Optional list of additional people involved in the deal beyond the primary contact, such as legal, security, or procurement, so they can be included on communications or internal routing.
parameters.name: participants

schema.description: Optional list of additional people involved in the deal beyond the primary contact—such as legal, security, or procurement—so they can be included on communications or internal routing.

role.description: Which side of the negotiation this person represents: `Customer` (buyer organization), `Supplier` (vendor organization), or `Vendr` (Vendr team).

parameters.description: Email of the primary stakeholder on the buyer side, the main person Vendr should treat as owner of this negotiation for questions and updates.
parameters.name: contact_email

parameters.description: Full name of the primary buyer contact (paired with `contactEmail`).
parameters.name: contact_name

parameters.description: How your organization wants Vendr engaged on this opportunity. `vendr_led` means Vendr drives the negotiation workflow end to end. `strategy_only` means advisory or strategic support without Vendr acting as the full execution owner of the negotiation.
parameters.name: engagement_type

parameters.description: Additional structured scope. Use the documented fields.
parameters.name: scope

schema.description: Optional commercial and timing context. All nested fields are optional; send the subset that you have so negotiators understand spend, dates, targets, and constraints.

additionalNotes.description: Any other unstructured context—SKU lists, quote references, compliance needs, or stakeholder notes—that helps scope the negotiation.

currentAnnualSpend.description: Approximate current annual contract value or recurring spend in major currency units (for example USD). Especially useful for renewals to anchor benchmarks.

dealType.description: High-level deal motion: `renewal` for an existing contract or relationship up for renewal, `new_purchase` for a net-new vendor or product purchase.

evaluatingAlternatives.description: Whether alternative vendors are being evaluated.

leverage.description: Free-text summary of negotiation leverage: alternatives, competitive bids, must-have dates, consolidation plans, or other factors that affect pricing power.

renewalDate.description: Key renewal, expiry, or decision date for the contract, as an ISO 8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD).

requirements.description: Free-text summary of the requirements for the negotiation. Product requirements, features, number of licenses, seats, etc.

targetPrice.description: Desired price point, budget cap, or goal the buyer is working toward for this deal (same currency convention as your internal quoting).

targetSignDate.description: Target sign date for intake (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO datetime); separate from renewal date on deal terms.

termInMonths.description: Expected or requested subscription term length in months (for example 12 or 36).

parameters.description: Additional structured file. Use the documented fields.
parameters.name: file

schema.description: Attach a document that was already uploaded for your organization via the file upload API. Omit this object when using multipart/form-data to send a new file in the same request as the JSON metadata.

fileId.description: UUID returned when the file was uploaded to your org. Must exist for the authenticated org or the request may fail with a file-not-found style error.

note.description: Short caption or explanation shown with the attachment (for example “Signed order form” or “Counterparty redlines”).

negotiationId.description: Unique id for the negotiation you just created. Use it with other Negotiation API paths (for example negotiation summary) or when correlating events in your systems.
